comparator.name: International Sociology
comparator.sourceNotes: Tilburg’s current official 2026–27 curriculum accounts for exactly 180 ECTS. Year 1 is a fixed 60-ECTS international-sociology foundation. Year 2 combines 36 ECTS of common methods, philosophy and research with the 24-ECTS Culture in Comparative Perspective major. The selected non-exchange Year 3 route contains a 12-ECTS internship, an 18-ECTS minor, 12 ECTS of Sociology electives, a 12-ECTS thesis and 6 ECTS of Social Philosophy. This is the published route used to complete the curriculum without inventing exchange or elective content.

routeSelection.basis: International Sociology explicitly uses an international and comparative perspective and offers two majors. Culture in Comparative Perspective directly continues that defining comparative identity and is listed first in the official curriculum. It is selected independently of UCR fit.

core: Sociological theories of social interaction, institutions, cohesion and social change
Social inequality, poverty, exclusion, welfare and urban life
Qualitative, quantitative and mixed sociological research using surveys, statistics and projects
Relationships among individuals, groups, institutions, society and public policy
Academic sociological craft and independent research culminating in a thesis
adjacent: Public policy, institutions and collective responses to social problems
Migration, culture, family and identities in comparative perspective
Climate, health, work and sustainability as social risks in changing societies
questions: What structures and mechanisms produce inequality and changing social problems?
How do institutions, culture and collective action reproduce or change social relations?
How can qualitative and quantitative evidence explain social patterns and change?

alternatives.label: International sociology, culture, identity & migration
alternatives.concept: Studies migration, cultural difference, family, identity and inequality through comparative sociology, histories of empire and gender, global political economy and transnational politics.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme centres international and comparative sociology, migration, culture, identity, empire and transnational relations while retaining a coherent research sequence.
progression: Sociology, politics, history and research foundations precede global political economy, migration-related inequality, race, citizenship, identity, international law and advanced transnational analysis. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Global social risks, health & sustainability
alternatives.concept: Examines how globalisation, climate change, migration, public health, work and governance create and distribute social risks, combining sociology with sustainability science, public economics, psychology and policy analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed programme integrates sociology with globalisation, climate, migration, health, sustainability governance, welfare economics and public communication around changing social risks.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest programme, this route replaces most historical, legal and transnational-culture content with sustainability foundations, climate science, sustainability governance, public economics, public health and climate communication. It differs by at least eight courses.
progression: Sociology, sustainability, health, research and statistics foundations precede climate communication, public economics, governance, political psychology and advanced applied research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: International inequality, policy & social research
alternatives.concept: Builds a sociological programme around comparative inequality, institutions, public policy and collective responses to social problems, supported by qualitative inquiry, statistics, data analysis and an applied research sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum contains the full available UCR sociology sequence plus comparative inequality, institutions, public policy and a substantial qualitative and quantitative research spine.
progression: Introductory sociology, institutions, research and statistics precede modern theory, inequality, qualitative and quantitative analysis, public health, global relations and advanced social research. All prerequisites and planned offerings pass; seven 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the culture-and-migration and social-risks routes, this programme gives greater weight to comparative institutions, policy, quantitative evidence, political economy and public communication. It differs from each earlier route by at least eight courses.

selection.assessment: The closest programme uses the complete available UCR sociology sequence and implements the selected international-comparative culture route. The global-social-risks and international-inequality/policy directions are independently supported by generator-eligible programme interests and the official curriculum, produce substantively different course choices, and pass feasibility and pairwise distinctness. Production therefore stops at the three-alternative maximum.

notes.text: Tilburg International Sociology provides a continuous disciplinary sequence in theory, qualitative and quantitative methods, survey construction, causal analysis, major-specific courses, sociological research projects and a 12-ECTS thesis. UCR offers a coherent sociology core and strong related study in politics, history, psychology, economics, media, sustainability and research methods, but it does not reproduce the same continuous specialist sociology sequence.

UCR does not reproduce Tilburg’s dedicated survey-construction course, full causal-analysis sequence, 12-ECTS second-year sociological research project, complete Culture in Comparative Perspective major, internship structure or 12-ECTS sociology thesis. Those differences remain explicit rather than being filled with weak substitutes.
